clue.text: Politician in severe pain swallowed first of drugs — it's difficult

indicators.note: in says the politician sits inside the word for severe pain

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain
MP is a Member of Parliament
swallowed means ate

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of drugs

explanation.surface: A politician doubled up in agony after taking drugs finds life hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate and hard to deal with is difficult; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe potter's cue dishearteningly touches pack first

indicators.note: touches means the next pieces sit right up against the first one
taking the heart out of cue removes its middle letter

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes
to ram is to pack tightly
1st written with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A snooker potter's cue lightly taps the pack of reds on the break.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker misleads: a potter here makes pots of clay. 'dishearteningly' leaves CE from cue; 'touches' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter is one example of an artist working in fired clay, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Marketing strategy, stolen by daily newspaper, succeeded

parts.note: the Daily Mail is a British newspaper
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A newspaper pinches someone's marketing plan and it works.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass mailing of advertising material is a direct-marketing tactic.

clue.text: Slow and fast over

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Something that is slow and also fast, and finished, a deliberate paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical tempo marking means to be played slowly, an Italian term.

clue.text: Camp's chilled Italian wine variable

parts.note: chilled means cold
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
Z is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A camp's chilled Italian wine varies in quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The German castle held Allied officers as a prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Hotel different without entrance it's said

indicators.note: without entrance drops the opening letter of the word for different

parts.note: other means different

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken, spelt by its sound

parts.note: it's spoken sounds like the letters entered

explanation.surface: A hotel that is different but has no front door, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without entrance' turns OTHER into THER; 'said' gives ITZ for 'it's'. The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London's Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous London establishment on Piccadilly is a grand hotel.

clue.text: Passing time, criticise rickety stairs, say

parts.note: passing is a euphemism for dying
to rap is to rebuke or criticise

explanation.surface: Someone passing time grumbles about a shaky staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickety stairs are an example of a dangerous structure likely to cause a fatal accident.

clue.text: Constant steer involved in this job?

definitions.text: Constant steer involved in this job?

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as for the speed of light
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: A question asking which job involves non-stop steering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a rowing crew's cox steers the boat constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing the person in the stern steers the boat throughout the race.

clue.text: Vehicle hogging A6 is a symbol of luxury

indicators.note: hogging means the vehicle holds the next piece in its middle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
A as written, then 6 as the Roman numeral VI

explanation.surface: A car hogging the A6 road is a show of opulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The A6 is a major British road, misleading the solver; here it is A plus VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is a famously expensive delicacy associated with luxurious living.

clue.text: Letter of affection, and sprayed in gold, creating blissful state

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: in means the shuffled word sits inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: sprayed suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A love letter sprayed with gold brings happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprayed' shuffles the word and into NAD before 'in' places it within gold's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Kubla Khan made the name stand for an idyllic, paradisal place or state.

clue.text: Regularly greeting unknown number, as monarchs do

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of greeting, the even ones

parts.note: n is the mathematician's unknown number

explanation.surface: Monarchs routinely greet a stream of strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings and queens rule over their realm, which is the verb sense here.

clue.text: Good book, in the main, on actor Bruce, old Hollywood star

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the following pieces come after

parts.note: Bruce Lee was the martial-arts film actor

indicators.note: in puts the version of the Bible inside the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea; main taken as written
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: A Bible at sea, carried by Bruce Lee, makes a Hollywood great.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actor famed for tough-guy roles was a film star of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Discussed physical strength in one despot

indicators.note: discussed means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: muscle is physical strength; in gives IN; I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the brute strength that lies in a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'muscle in I' sounds like the dictator's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Fascist dictator ruled Italy as an autocratic tyrant.

clue.text: Ring kept in firm's hidden stock

indicators.note: kept in says the ring is held within the word for firm

parts.note: firm means hard
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wedding ring is kept in a company's secret stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache or secret stash of goods kept for the future, like a squirrel's store.

clue.text: How's new French composer avoiding alien world of entertainment

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
avoiding means the alien is left out of the composer's name

parts.note: Georges Bizet, composer of Carmen
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Asking how a new French composer avoids an alien world of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Show business is the entertainment industry; the short form is informal.

clue.text: Inflatable, in principle, boosts every party

indicators.note: a principle is a beginning or source, so it takes the first letter of boosts

parts.note: every means each
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: An inflatable, in theory, livens up any party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as 'in theory' but means the origin, the first letter of 'boosts'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun inflatable covers blow-up toys such as the large ball used at the seaside.

clue.text: Nothing in minor e-zine recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words minor e-zine

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Nothing in a small online magazine is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link, but it is the hiding signal; 'recalled' then reads the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure for nothing is a nought, a synonym in counting.

clue.text: Reflecting, one local with left hand approved vegetable

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a local is a pub, a bar
OK means approved

explanation.surface: Musing, a pub regular with a left hand gives a vegetable the nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' turns IBARLHOK round. A local is British for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip cabbage, a swollen-stemmed brassica, is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Perhaps badger Edward to restrain upsetting work culture

indicators.note: to restrain means Edward's short name holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

indicators.note: upsetting, in a down clue, turns the string upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
art is culture

explanation.surface: Edward should badger his firm to curb a troubling work culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses OPART to TRAPO, which goes inside TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger is one example of a four-legged vertebrate, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Jack joins sleepy characters on a music class

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the sleepy letters come after

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
ZZ represents snoring in cartoons

explanation.surface: Jack joins some drowsy figures in a music lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a class, and this is a genre of music born in New Orleans.

clue.text: Olympic champion, to exercise core in workout, goes to extremes

indicators.note: goes to means the following pieces come after the extremes

parts.note: A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet, here Z then A
PE is physical education

indicators.note: core in takes the middle letter of workout

explanation.surface: An Olympic champion pushes a workout to extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes' points at the alphabet's ends, Z and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech distance runner won three golds at the 1952 Helsinki Games.

clue.text: Fly with fellow editor westwards — this helps to find location in LA?

definitions.text: this helps to find location in LA?

parts.note: to fly is to zip along
co- is a prefix for a fellow, as in co-worker

indicators.note: westwards in an across clue means read right to left

explanation.surface: A fly travels west with a fellow editor, looking for a Los Angeles address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in LA' signals American usage: a US postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: The US postal number lets mail be routed to an address, like a British postcode.

clue.text: Most mad finding a metallic element in relish

indicators.note: in places the a and element inside the word for relish

parts.note: zest is relish or gusto
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A chemist madly discovers a metal in a pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means comically mad, so its superlative is most mad.

clue.text: Football chiefs left cold, playing predator

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
on means playing, as an actor is on

explanation.surface: Football bosses left out in the cold while playing a ruthless rival.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird of prey hunts other birds, a predator.

clue.text: Times defends current publication about crime

indicators.note: defends means the word for times surrounds the others

parts.note: by means times, as in 3 by 4
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: about means the publication is turned round

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: The Times defends a topical magazine story about a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married is a criminal offence in many countries.

clue.text: Alpha male vaguely belonging to religious sect

parts.note: A is alpha in the radio alphabet
-ish is a suffix meaning vaguely or roughly

explanation.surface: An alpha male loosely attached to a religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anabaptist group known for plain living is a religious sect; the adjective describes its members.

clue.text: Run with Ellen, oddball revolutionary who tried to escape from 4?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a nut is an eccentric, an oddball

explanation.surface: Ellen and an eccentric revolutionary are on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is COLDITZ, the prisoner-of-war camp, and prisoners dug tunnels to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners at the camp dug under the walls, hoping to break out.

clue.text: Follow Alsatian in, with "Beg!"

parts.note: en is French for in, as spoken in Alsace
to sue is to beg or plead

explanation.surface: Telling an Alsatian dog to come in and beg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alsatian looks like the dog; it is someone from Alsace, a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result is to follow.

clue.text: Fruit item from bakery available in fancy parcel

indicators.note: available in says the bread roll is to be found inside the other letters
fancy implies the letters are elaborately rearranged

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

explanation.surface: Fruit and baked goods are on offer in a pretty parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the word parcel into CRAPLE. A bap is British for a soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The small, sour wild apple is a fruit.

clue.text: Boggy land, area commoner on Devon Cornwall peninsula

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the area and commoner come after

parts.note: SW, the South West peninsula of England holding Devon and Cornwall
an MP sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Marshland and a commoner's patch in the far South West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterlogged ground such as a bog or marsh.

clue.text: Some, putting name forward, vote negatively

indicators.note: putting with forward says a letter is shifted toward the front
forward tells us the abbreviation moves to the start

parts.note: any means some

explanation.surface: Some put a candidate's name forward but then vote against it.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for no is a vote against, as in the ayes and the noes.

clue.text: Enjoy article finally penned after victory: How Usain Bolt runs?

indicators.note: after says the pen's end comes behind the victory

parts.note: to like is to enjoy
the is the definite article
a win is a victory

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of penned

explanation.surface: A reporter enjoys an article finally written about a win: the sprinter's speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jamaican sprinter famously runs extremely fast, an idiom for great speed.
